question.text: A double top chart pattern suggests:

answer.text: A bullish continuation of the uptrend
A bearish reversal with two failed attempts to break above a resistance level

explanation.text: The Logic: A double top is a classic reversal chart pattern. Price rallies to a resistance area, pulls back, then attempts that same resistance level a second time. When the second attempt also fails to break through, it signals that buyers are exhausted and sellers are taking control — pointing to a bearish reversal of the prior uptrend. The pattern is typically confirmed when price subsequently breaks below the intervening trough (neckline). The Trap: A bullish continuation is the opposite of what a double top signals — the pattern indicates the uptrend is failing. A neutral sideways range does not capture the failed-resistance and reversal dynamic. A rise in trading volume is not what the price pattern itself describes; volume is a confirming tool, not the meaning of the pattern. Note: The specific double-top chart-pattern definition above is not stated on the cited NISM Series XV Research Analyst pages checked (pp.310, 313, 319, 325) — p.319 only references MACD "double top or bottom" in the context of the MACD indicator. The framing above reflects general industry technical-analysis usage.
